key_insight: LLM-driven evolutionary program search improves generative retrieval by optimizing semantic identifier construction and collision handling.
engineering_relevance: A locally served open-weight 31B model and a 1M-parameter proxy decoder enable component search without proprietary LLM APIs or repeated training of the 1B target generator.
method: Use an LLM to mutate executable generative retrieval components.
Score candidate programs with a lightweight proxy decoder.
Transfer promising semantic index designs to the target generator under a fixed training recipe.
evidence_signal: On NQ320K, proxy and target Recall@100 rankings correlated strongly across 21 SID programs (Spearman ρ=0.90); jointly evolving SID construction and collision handling raised Recall@1 from 55.8% to 59.3% and Recall@100 from 85.8% to 90.6%.
watch_item: Validate proxy reliability for each search space: gains transferred reliably for semantic index evolution, but not for training-objective or full-pipeline evolution.
paper_title: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval
